audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Public Administration and Organisation Science degree studies how governments and public organisations make decisions, deliver services and respond to social problems. Students study policy, law and management and conduct research in organisations.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The listed courses and profiling space account for 180 EC. The entry rules for qualitative research and the graduation project still need confirmation before a complete comparison can be shown.

curriculum.limitation: Utrecht requires at least 15 EC at advanced level within profiling and 15 EC in an international context across the degree. The entry rules for qualitative research and the graduation project remain unverified for September 2026 entrants.

componentNotes.bo-y2-choice: This 7.5 EC elective is part of the 37.5 EC profiling space.
componentNotes.bo-y2-qualitative: Students use interviews and observations to investigate a question from an organisation.
componentNotes.bo-y3-profiling: Four 7.5 EC choices. At least 15 EC of the full 37.5 EC profiling space must be at advanced level.
componentNotes.bo-y3-capstone: Students analyse a public issue and write an advisory report. Utrecht lists Organisations in Transition and Policy, Rationality and Power as prerequisites.
componentNotes.bo-y3-thesis: Students prepare an individual research project in period three and carry it out and write the thesis in period four.
componentNotes.bo-y2-institutions: This 7.5 EC major course is taught in English and includes a paper in English.

exception.reason: Utrecht’s public course listings refer to progression regulations for entry to qualitative research and the graduation project. The applicable entry rules for September 2026 entrants still need confirmation.
exception.curriculumContext: The three-year degree lists a 142.5 EC major and 37.5 EC of profiling, including a 22.5 EC graduation project within the major. Profiling requires at least 15 advanced EC. The degree requires 15 EC in an international context. The qualitative research and graduation project entry requirements remain unresolved.
